sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: While corporate boardrooms and political campaigns frequently use the language of women's empowerment, true gender equality remains restricted by deep structural barriers and unacknowledged economic imbalances. The primary factor driving this inequality is the vast, unequal distribution of unpaid care work—including domestic labor, childcare, and eldercare—which falls disproportionately on women. This massive expenditure of time acts as a structural barrier to career advancement, forcing women into precarious, informal employment and driving the persistent gender wage gap. Furthermore, simple institutional inclusion, such as meeting gender quotas in employment, is often used as a superficial fix that fails to change deeply entrenched patriarchal workplace cultures. True structural empowerment requires far more than just entry into the workforce; it demands comprehensive state infrastructure, such as subsidized universal childcare, parental leave systems that encourage equal participation by men, and strong legal protections against workplace discrimination. Gender equality cannot be achieved by asking women to adapt to systems built for men; it requires entirely dismantling and rebuilding those institutional structures.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The vastness of the universe, with its billions of galaxies and innumerable stars, fuels ongoing speculation about the existence of extraterrestrial life. Astrobiology, the scientific discipline dedicated to studying life's potential beyond Earth, integrates astronomy, biology, and geology to explore this profound question. Despite decades of observation and advances in space exploration, definitive evidence of alien life remains elusive. However, discoveries of extremophiles on Earth — organisms thriving in conditions previously thought uninhabitable — expand the conceivable habitats where life might exist elsewhere. Furthermore, the identification of exoplanets within habitable zones around distant stars has intensified the search for biosignatures indicative of life. The Fermi Paradox, highlighting the contradiction between the high probability of extraterrestrial civilizations and the lack of contact, emphasizes the complexities of this quest. Reasons for the paradox range from the rarity of advanced life to limits on interstellar communication or travel. As technology progresses, initiatives like the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (SETI) and upcoming space missions aim to unravel these cosmic mysteries, underscoring humanity's profound curiosity about our place in the cosmos.

questions.q: The author identifies which of the following as a major structural barrier to women's career advancement?
opts: Gender quotas that artificially accelerate corporate inclusion.
Women's lack of adaptability in traditional workplaces.
The absence of political representation and awareness campaigns.
The disproportionate burden of unpaid care work and domestic labour.
questions.why: Detail: unpaid care work 'acts as a structural barrier to career advancement'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The passage suggests that institutional gender quotas often function as:
opts: A way to remove the need for universal childcare.
The main driver of the gender wage gap.
A superficial solution that fails to alter entrenched workplace cultures.
A radical reform that instantly ends patriarchal systems.
questions.why: Inference: quotas are 'a superficial fix that fails to change deeply entrenched patriarchal workplace cultures'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the text, the gender wage gap is heavily driven by women being forced into:
opts: Technical fields that reject empowerment rhetoric.
Precarious, informal employment due to the time demands of unpaid care work.
Executive roles that lack parental leave.
questions.why: Detail: stated in the third sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a requirement for genuine structural empowerment?
opts: Subsidized universal childcare and parental leave that engages men equally.
Replacing public childcare with corporate self-regulation.
Teaching women to navigate workplaces built for men.
Restricting women's employment to formal boardrooms.
questions.why: Detail: listed under 'comprehensive state infrastructure'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The central argument of the passage is that gender equality:
opts: Requires rebuilding institutional structures rather than asking women to adapt to them.
Has been achieved through corporate quotas.
Should be left to individual negotiation in the private sector.
Is unattainable because care work is naturally divided.
questions.why: Main idea: the last sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “It is high time we ______ the old files.”
questions.why: 'It is high time' + subject + past tense (subjunctive). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Spot the error: “Either the clerk or the officers is responsible for the delay.”
questions.why: With either/or, the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('officers'): 'are'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “Who wrote this letter?”
opts: By whom was this letter written?
By whom was written this letter?
By whom this letter was written?
questions.why: Question form: By whom + was + subject + past participle. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “She ______ in this hospital since 2015.”
questions.why: An action from a past point continuing now, with 'since': present perfect (continuous). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct idiom: “The new scheme was a great success.” (meaning)
questions.why: 'Take off' = become successful; 'fall flat' and 'fall through' = fail. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.why: Passed in August 2026, the 150th year of the song.

questions.why: UN General Assembly resolution, 2007.

questions.why: Windergy India 2026 was held in Chennai, Oct 2026.

questions.q: The draft notification of July 2026 declares about 56,826 sq km of the Western Ghats eco-sensitive across how many states?
questions.why: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: IMEC, in news in 2026, is the India–Middle East–Europe:
questions.why: Announced at the G20 New Delhi summit, 2023.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 5, 11, 23, 47, 95, ?
questions.why: Each term is double the previous one plus 1: 95 x 2 + 1 = 191.

questions.q: If ROAD is written as URDG in a certain code, how is FORT written?
questions.why: Each letter moves three places forward: F-I, O-R, R-U, T-W.

questions.q: Odometer is to distance as barometer is to:
questions.why: An odometer measures distance travelled; a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.q: A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. How is A related to D?
questions.why: A is the daughter of C, and C is the daughter of D, so A is D's granddaughter.

questions.q: A man walks 4 km south, turns left and walks 3 km, then turns left again and walks 8 km. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.why: He ends 3 km east and 4 km north of the start. The straight-line distance is 5 km, to the north-east.

questions.q: Ravi is 12th from the top and 19th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in the class?
questions.why: Total = 12 + 19 - 1 = 30, which is not among options A to D.

questions.q: Sam bought 20 dozen toys at ₹375 a dozen and sold each toy for ₹33. What was his profit per cent?
questions.why: Cost per toy 375 ÷ 12 = 31.25; profit 1.75; 1.75 ÷ 31.25 = 5.6%. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: 60% of a school's students are boys. 25% of the boys and 30% of the girls hold scholarships. What per cent of all students hold scholarships?
Find the sum of the first 30 even natural numbers.
Find the wrong number in the series: 582, 605, 588, 611, 634, 617, 600
questions.why: The pattern is +23, −17 by turns: 611 − 17 = 594, not 634. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: The hallmark of irreversible cell injury is:
opts: Nuclear changes such as karyolysis and pyknosis
questions.why: Swelling and fatty change are reversible.

questions.q: Caseous necrosis is characteristic of:
questions.why: Cheese-like necrosis within granulomas.

questions.q: The first cells to arrive at a site of acute inflammation are usually:
questions.why: Neutrophils dominate the first 6–24 hours.

questions.q: The cardinal signs of inflammation described by Celsus are rubor, tumor, calor and:
questions.why: Virchow later added loss of function.

questions.q: Virchow's triad for thrombosis includes endothelial injury, abnormal blood flow (stasis) and:
questions.why: The three factors predisposing to thrombosis.

questions.q: The commonest type of embolism is:
questions.why: Most arise from deep vein thrombosis of the legs.

questions.q: A benign tumour of glandular epithelium is called:
questions.why: Malignant glandular tumours are adenocarcinomas.

questions.q: Metastasis by the lymphatic route is typical of:
questions.why: Sarcomas usually spread by blood.

questions.q: The causative organism of typhoid fever is:
questions.why: Enteric fever is caused by Salmonella Typhi and Paratyphi.

questions.q: In the first week of typhoid fever, the most useful investigation is:
questions.why: Blood culture is positive in the first week; Widal rises in the second.

questions.q: Dengue fever is transmitted by:
questions.why: A day-biting mosquito.

questions.q: The most dangerous species of malarial parasite, causing cerebral malaria, is:
questions.why: It causes cerebral malaria and severe anaemia.

questions.q: The gold standard for diagnosing malaria is:
questions.why: Thick and thin smears stained by Giemsa or Leishman.

questions.q: Hepatitis B infection is indicated by the presence in serum of:
questions.why: Hepatitis B surface antigen.

questions.q: The stain used to identify Mycobacterium tuberculosis in sputum is:
questions.why: Acid-fast bacilli stain red.

questions.q: Under India's TB programme, the preferred initial test for diagnosing pulmonary TB is now:
questions.why: Nucleic acid amplification tests also detect rifampicin resistance.

questions.q: Normal haemoglobin in an adult male is about:
questions.why: Around 12–15 g/dL in women.

questions.q: A raised eosinophil count is typically seen in:
questions.why: Asthma, allergy and worm infestation.

questions.q: Thrombocytopenia is a common laboratory finding in:
questions.why: The platelet count is monitored in dengue.

questions.q: The ESR is raised in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.why: Polycythaemia lowers the ESR.

questions.q: A rise of serum ALT (SGPT) mainly indicates:
questions.why: ALT is fairly liver-specific.

questions.q: Raised serum creatinine and blood urea most often point to:
questions.why: Both are part of the renal function tests.

questions.q: Ketone bodies in urine with glycosuria suggest:
questions.why: Also seen in starvation, but with glycosuria think DKA.

questions.q: Air under the diaphragm on an erect chest X-ray indicates:
questions.why: Pneumoperitoneum, as in perforated peptic ulcer.

questions.q: The investigation of choice for suspected gallstones is:
questions.why: Most gallstones are not radio-opaque.
